subject: RFP: Dedicated capacity — throughput projection & burst plan
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily@sigmanalytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sigmanalytics.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: RFP - Dedicated capacity: throughput profiling and burst questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Sigma Analytics' RFP we need a clearer sense of how you’d size a dedicated pool for our primary inference workloads. High level profile:~500 concurrent chat sessions (max), typical prompt + response 1,200 tokens, average session generates ~6k tokens/day, embeddings workload for search at ~20 QPS (short vectors).

Key asks:
- Recommended GPU mix for a 12-month committed pool (we run both latency-critical chat and cheaper embedding pipelines)
- Expected steady-state tokens/sec per GPU for our two main model families (a 13B decoder model and a 70B decoder model, quantized where applicable)
- How you handle burst demand (3x baseline for marketing spikes) without breaking latency SLOs
- Proc steps & timeline for reserved capacity commits + DocuSign cadence

I've attached the RFP worksheet (RFP_Sigma_v1.xlsx). Can you review and send a preliminary sizing by next week? Procurement is copied for timelines.

Appreciate it — Emily

Attachment: RFP_Sigma_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@sigmanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@sigmanalytics.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:28:00-04:00
Subject: Re: RFP - Dedicated capacity: throughput profiling and burst questions

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear profile and the worksheet. High-level notes up front, and I attached a capacity snapshot that lays out a conservative starting recommendation.

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_v3.xlsx (xlsx)

Summary (executive):
- Recommended commit (baseline): 4 x H100 nodes (latency-critical chat), 12 x A100-80GB (cost-effective LLM serving), 6 x L4-class instances (embeddings + lightweight pre/post-processing).
- Baseline throughput estimate: using model assumptions below, baseline system supports ~2.8M tokens/min overall (~46.5k tokens/sec) across the pool.
- Burst plan: enable a 3x burst window via pre-warmed burst pool and autoscaling to burst capacity for up to 90 minutes; warm pools are kept idle but with cached model weights for fast spin-up.
- Latency objective: target p50 < 200ms and p95 < 600ms for chat when routed to H100 + continuous batching; A100 paths optimized for higher throughput with p95 up to 900ms for the large 70B model.

Assumptions used (please confirm):
- Chat model: 13B decoder (quantized), average seq-in/out 1.2k tokens, batching window 15-30ms for latency paths.
- Long-form model: 70B decoder (Q4 quantized), used for higher-quality completions at lower QPS.
- Embeddings: dense small model on L4-class instances; embedding QPS ~20 with small contexts.

Questions for you:
1) Do the 500 concurrent sessions map to always-on users or do some sessions idle for long polling?
2) Any regulatory or region-specific constraints for cross-region fallback?
3) Target latency SLOs for p99 (we usually design for p95 but can dimension for p99 with additional H100 capacity).

I'll loop Marcus on detailed GPU throughput profiling and Rishi on network/fallback architecture. If that timeline works, we can lock numbers and produce an offer and SLA draft next week.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Director, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP - Dedicated capacity: throughput profiling and burst questions

Emily / Grace — digging into the technical sizing and tradeoffs below. I'll try to keep the math readable — happy to run the same worksheet through your exact token distributions.

Per-GPU throughput (ballpark, under our inference runtime with continuous batching and KV caching):
- H100 (4x NVLink, 80GB static): ~18k - 25k tokens/sec for a quantized 13B chat model under low-latency batching (small batch windows). For the 70B quantized model, H100 gives ~3.5k - 5k tokens/sec.
- A100 80GB: ~10k - 14k tokens/sec for the 13B quantized model; ~2.0k - 3.0k tokens/sec for the 70B quantized model.
- L4-class (GPU server with 24GB class): optimized for embeddings; ~3000 small-vector embeddings/sec (depends on vector dim and batching).

Sizing rationale using your profile:
- Baseline chat load: 500 concurrent sessions with 1.2k tokens average -> concurrent token generation at peak roughly 600k tokens/min = 10k tokens/sec. Accounting for variance and headroom we recommend baseline 2x capacity headroom -> 20k tokens/sec baseline for chat.
- Using the H100 numbers above, 2 x H100 nodes could support ~36k - 50k tokens/sec for 13B low-latency paths — but we recommend 4 H100s to give conservative headroom for p95/p99 spikes, autoscaling buffer and to run canary/rollout instances.
- For heavy 70B usage: reserve 6 A100s; they are more cost-effective for sustained throughput on large models where latency requirements are laxer.

Burst strategy:
- Warm pool approach: maintain a small set of pre-warmed instances per model (cached weights in GPU RAM) so spin-up is <20s. For bursts we pre-allocate a hot-burst pool (pay-as-you-reserve) sized for 2x baseline and a policy to spill over to regionally compatible spare capacity.
- Cache & batching: prefix KV cache for common system prompts will cut duplicate work; intelligent batching windows expand slightly during bursts to increase throughput while preserving p95 SLAs via routing rules.

Reservation planning / commit guidance:
- 12-month phased commit: Start with the baseline recommended above (4 H100 / 12 A100 / 6 L4). Phase ramp at months: 0-3 baseline, 4-6 +25% capacity, 7-12 evaluation and add burst pool if utilization >70%.
- We also recommend a small on-demand buffer (10-15% of capacity) for unexpected peaks; that reduces idle committed spend but preserves SLOs.

Network & high-availability notes (Rishi can add details):
- Cross-region fallback: replicate critical models to a secondary region; automated routing should failover to compatible quantized variants if a region is unhealthy.
- Minimum network egress for lab workloads to meet your compliance requirements is documented in the network diagram (Grace will attach).

I'll prepare a one-page worksheet with the numbers inserted into your RFP file if that's useful.

— Marcus

Thanks Marcus, Grace — this is very helpful. A few clarifying items for procurement and architecture before we move to commit: 

1) Cold start concerns: if a burst requires loading the 70B model onto A100s, can the "warm pool" guarantee <60s readiness for full model on A100, or will we need the H100 pool for fast bursts?
2) Cross-region failover: we operate primarily in us-west-2 but require a failover option in us-east-1; any implications for model sync and added storage costs?
3) Pricing ask: can you share a redline example for a 12-month commit with quarterly ramp steps and a documented burst-credit arrangement? Procurement is specifically asking for DocuSign-ready terms.

Procurement note: we can start negotiation on standard reserved capacity terms but need to confirm SLA language around p95 and scheduled maintenance windows.

If you can send a short SLA draft and the revised worksheet with the warm-pool ramp timeline, we can get internal approval to proceed to DocuSign.

Regards,
Emily

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@sigmanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@sigmanalytics.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP - Dedicated capacity: throughput profiling and burst questions

Emily / procurement team — thanks, and apologies for the slight delay. Attached: SLA draft and a short network diagram. Below are concrete answers and a suggested mutual-action plan.

Attachments:
- ml-inference-sla-draft.pdf (pdf)
- network-diagram.png (png)

Answers:
- Cold starts and warm pool: for 70B on A100, warm-pool best-effort brings readiness to ~45–60s depending on concurrency of pulls; we recommend using H100-backed low-latency pool for any sub-60s hard SLOs. For most marketing bursts (90-120 minutes) the A100 warm pool is sufficient; we can include an "emergency H100 burst" clause for true p99-critical flows.
- Cross-region: model replication to us-east-1 adds storage cost (S3 + encrypted snapshots) and bandwidth but is supported. We typically recommend asynchronous replication with a ~15–30 minute recovery window for large model artifacts.
- Pricing & DocuSign: Neha will attach a redline offer, but our standard 12-month phased commit template with burst credits is included in the HubSpot deal link. We can deliver a DocuSign package within 3 business days once countersigned internally.

Mutual action plan (MAP):
- July 13: Redwood to provide final redline and DocuSign package (owner: Neha)
- July 16: Sigma to confirm baseline commit and sign PO (owner: Emily / procurement)
- July 20: Enable baseline dedicated pool (owner: Redwood infra); 0-3 day provisioning SLA for initial capacity
- Aug 1: Begin phased ramp step 1 (+25% capacity) if utilization >60% (owner: Sigma/Redwood)

Commit suggestion: start with the baseline we outlined (4 H100 / 12 A100 / 6 L4) on a 12-month contract with quarterly usage reviews and a one-time burst credit pool (equivalent to 15% monthly baseline compute) applied during month 1–3.

Next steps: I’ll drop the SLA + network diagram into the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign once Neha finishes the redline. Want to book a 30-minute run-through next week to confirm ramp dates? I’m proposing July 14 at 10am PT.

Best regards,
Grace O'Connor
Account Director, Redwood Inference
